title: Training load
subtitle: What your activities add up to: fatigue, fitness and form
loadFailed: Could not load your training load

sources.title: Sources
sources.matrixNote: The same activity scored by every signal that could read it: watts are measured; gradient-compensated pace and heart rate are estimates.

rapNote: RAP = grade-equivalent pace: the actual pace corrected for gradient, which is the pace the pace-side formulas score.

daily.trimpNote: TRIMP uses a different scale than the other formulas and is never added to them.
daily.danielsNote: Daniels points use a scale of their own and are never added to the other formulas.
daily.rssNote: aRSS measures only activities that carry power. An activity without power stays out of this series; heart-rate load is what measures it.
daily.bandNote: The bands say where the work happened: climbs, high, middle, low. Each powered second counts in exactly one band, so they add up to aRSS total.

empty.title: No load measured yet
empty.description: Once your activities have been measured, your fitness and fatigue curves will appear here. You can queue the measurement from the settings below.

settings.ivHint: Interval knobs are compared with your own numbers (threshold and each session's median). Blank means the default.
settings.paceSmoothHint: The seconds the pace-side score averages over: larger smooths more GPS noise but also absorbs short surges (default 20 s).

actions.refreshHint: Re-derives CP/W′ and threshold heart rate from your records; manual values are kept.
actions.recomputeHint: Re-measures every activity with the current thresholds and formula; do it after changing either.

power.subtitle: Your highest sustained averages and the critical power derived from them

empty.title: No curve for this sport yet
empty.description: The curve appears once activities with power for this sport have been measured.

power.balanceHint: Choose an activity to see how its efforts consumed and recovered W′.
power.balanceEmpty: This sport needs a fitted W′ to draw the balance; totals above the threshold are still shown.
power.flagsNotice: {count} sessions held out of the curve for implausible peaks

intervals.title: Interval analysis
intervals.basis: Everything is measured against your own numbers: threshold {threshold} and this session's median {base}.
intervals.tcNote: Climbs are read from the terrain, whatever the power did; they may overlap the timeline and are never summed with it. aRSS needs a power meter. "≈" is estimated from gradient-compensated pace or heart rate when the activity has no power.
intervals.rules: How it is detected here: on the flat a stretch counts as an interval only if it holds ≥{effortIf}·CP; an effort opens at {openW} W and closes below {closeW} W; minimum {minS} s (under {shortS} s it needs {shortBase} the session median; with no real recovery —≤{recoveryW} W—, {strongBase}); a grade above {climbGrade}% with IF<{climbIf} counts as a climb.

trail.title: Technical sections
trail.summary: {technical}% of the ground ({metres} m of {of} m) reads as technical terrain.
trail.hint: Sections where the pace falls short of what the grade explains, with irregular stride and braking on descents. On the map they are drawn in amber, red where the detector is most confident. This detector is still being calibrated against real routes.
trail.clickHint: Pick a row to see the stretch on the map, or click a stretch on the map.
trail.mapMissingHint: No mapped way covers this stretch: the extract is missing or the ground is unmapped.
trail.markHint: Judge it when your memory disagrees: the verdicts are what the method is calibrated against, and they can be undone.

bestTimes.title: Best times
bestTimes.subtitle: Your fastest split over classic race distances, found in each activity's samples, with the split's power and a link to the day you ran it.

empty.title: No valid splits
empty.description: No stretch in the window passes the grade filter, or no activity has power.

bestTimes.note: Splits whose net grade falls below −1 % (−2 % under 800 m) are discarded: a downhill is not a personal best.

laps.rssNote: aRSS is the intensity-weighted score behind the daily load; the rows add up to the activity's total. "≈" is estimated from gradient-compensated pace or heart rate when the activity has no power.

cpTrend.title: Critical power evolution
cpTrend.note: One point per session, fitted from its own sustained efforts alone; how scattered the dots are reflects each session's quality, not the day's form. The dashed line is the temporal threshold those days' loads were scored against.
cpTrend.emptyDescription: Critical power needs sessions with at least four sustained efforts between 5 and 30 minutes. It fills in as you collect them.
cpTrend.loadingSlow: Reading the whole history; the first load can take a minute

trailNetwork.title: Trail network
trailNetwork.subtitle: Every mapped way you have crossed, judged only by your descents of it — the climb tells nothing.
trailNetwork.hint: The map draws one line per way, coloured by the claim its descents support. One way needs at least {min} descents before anything is claimed for it; the spread shows how much the crossings agree.

empty.title: No crossed ways yet
empty.description: A few descents of the same path accumulate the evidence this view needs.

trailNetwork.showPlain: Also draw crossed ways that carry no claim

variants.title: Route variants
variants.none: No reconnection alternative was found over ground you have already crossed.
variants.hint: Every variant comes from ground you have physically crossed yourself: mark it real when you have seen the ground is there, false when it is a GPS artifact. Denied variants never come back.

routes.title: Your routes
routes.subtitle: Routes designed over your own crossed ground. Save a run as a route to search its variants and, later, export it as a navigable course.
routes.downloadError: The course could not be downloaded.
routes.pickA: Click the map to pick the starting point
routes.generateError: The plan could not be generated. Two points too far apart, or no connection?
routes.deleteBody: "{name}" and its variant verdicts will be gone. This cannot be undone.

empty.title: No saved routes yet
empty.description: Open a run and press "Save as route" to start designing over your own ground.

routes.drawHint: Click the map to add route points. Click a point to remove it.
routes.snapHint: In fitted mode, stretches follow ground you have already crossed; stretches that cannot are saved as straight lines.
routes.connectFailed: The route could not be fitted to your ground. Try again, or save in free mode.
